The failure is caused by a bug in the frozen instrument ([policy.py](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L303-L318)), triggered when the driver pivots to a booking during a reschedule:

1. **Instrument bug (`fix`)**: In [`PatientPolicy._in_truth`](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L303-L318), the `"cancel"` branch checks `any(i["action"] == "cancel" for i in self.t["intents"])`, but the `"book"` branch only checks `self.now["schedule"]["works"]` (and self-pay limits) without checking `any(i["action"] == "book" for i in self.t["intents"])`. Because `reschedule_own` populates `schedule["works"]` with candidate slots for the move, the simulated patient answers `"Yes"` to a `"book"` offer even though their only intent is `"move"`.
2. **Trigger in the driver**: When a rambling patient picks a new time, [voice.py](file:///work/clinicbench/voice.py#L287-L288) appends `COLOR[0]` from [truth.py](file:///work/clinicbench/truth.py#L38) (`"I don't drive, so I'm going by my daughter's schedule"`). [`parse_intents`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L90-L104) matches `"schedule"` as `"book"`, and [`Driver.route`](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L340-L345) pivots the active `"reschedule"` workflow to `"book"`.

The failure is a bug in the frozen patient instrument (`clinicbench/policy.py`), so its kind is `fix`.

In [`PatientPolicy._in_truth`](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L303-L318), the `"book"` branch checks whether the offered slot is in `self.now["schedule"]["works"]` (and checks self-pay willingness/cap if `self_pay`), but unlike `"cancel"` it never checks whether `"book"` is actually in `self.t["intents"]`. Because move scenarios (`reschedule_own`, `unconfirmed_reschedule`) also populate `self.now["schedule"]["works"]` with valid new times for the existing appointment, [`PatientPolicy.respond_offer`](file:///work/clinicbench/policy.py#L320-L351) accepts a `"book"` read-back for one of those slots and answers yes, causing a second, new booking to be created while the original appointment remains untouched.

PatientPolicy._in_truth does not check that "book" is in self.t["intents"] when evaluating a "book" offer or read-back. Because a "move" patient has working slots populated in self.now["schedule"]["works"], they answer yes to confirm a new booking if the clinician offers one at their chosen time.

PatientPolicy._in_truth does not check that "book" is in self.t["intents"] when evaluating a "book" offer/read-back, and move scenarios also populate self.now["schedule"]["works"] with the new times. As a result, a patient intending only to move an existing appointment accepts a "book" confirmation for their chosen slot and ends up with a second, new booking.
